newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand's NESDB sees 1997 GDP growth at 7.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Thailand's NESDB sees 1997 GDP growth at 7.1 pct.

text.p: The Thai government's National Economic and Social Development Board (NESDB) said on Monday it expects 1997 gross domestic product (GDP) growth of 7.1 percent, up from its forecast of 6.8 percent in 1996.
The NESDB's 1997 projection matched the central bank's forecast last month. However, the central bank's prediction pegged 1996 growth at 6.7 percent.
The NESDB also projected the current account deficit to narrow to 7.7 percent of GDP against its own estimate of 8.3 percent for this year.
The Bank of Thailand had also seen a narrowing of the 1997 deficit to 7.9 of GDP versus a projected 8.2 percent in 1996.
The government think tank added that it expected the 1997 inflation growth rate to be 5.0 percent versus its own forecast of 5.9 percent for last year.

The projected inflation figure for 1997 was slightly higher than the forecast made by the central bank which had expected the growth to average 4.8 percent this year and projected 5.8 percent growth for 1996.
On exports growth, the NESDB forecast that they would grow 11.6 percent in 1997 versus its own projection of 0.2 percent made for 1996.

The central bank had seen 1997 exports growing far less at 7.7 percent and forecast a 0.1 percent contraction in growth for last year. This compared with 23.6 percent growth posted in 1995, the Bank of Thailand said.
The central bank is expected to finalise leading economic indicators for 1996 in February or March.
